title: Prompt to share installation info causes mcp-get to break in CI flows
body:
I'm trying to install `mcp-get` within a Dockerfile, to then use it to install an MCP server, which I can then serve with Docker. I'd like to keep everything dockerised so it aligns with the rest of our CI.

When I run `npx -y @michaellatman/mcp-get@latest install <mcp server package>`, the initial installation of `mcp-get` works successfully, but then the CLI returns a prompt:

```
Would you like to help improve mcp-get by sharing anonymous installation analytics? (Y/n) 
```

As far as I can tell, the `-y` flag that I have already included is only being used by `npx` to suppress any prompts relating to the installation of mcp-get, rather than any prompts that pop up related to mcp-get trying to install a particular MCP server package.

Are there any flags I can add to this command to ignore any prompts like this, so that I can use `mcp-get` within my CI pipeline?
author: nbailey-sigtech

comments.body: Good call. I can add that.

Thank you for your contribution! I've reviewed the PR and have the following findings:

### Package List JSON Format
 The package entry follows the correct JSON format
 All required fields are present (name, description, vendor, sourceUrl, homepage, license, runtime)
 Proper integration into the existing JSON structure

### Package Publication Status
 The package is not published to npm registry
- The package-list.json specifies "runtime": "node", which requires npm publication
- There's a discrepancy in the package name:
  - package-list.json uses: "mcp-server-mysql"
  - README.md references: "@benborla29/mcp-server-mysql"
  - Please ensure the package is published with the correct name and update package-list.json accordingly

### Environment Variables
 All required environment variables are properly configured in src/helpers/index.ts:
- MYSQL_HOST (required)
- MYSQL_PORT (optional, defaults to 3306)
- MYSQL_USER (required)
- MYSQL_PASS (required)
- MYSQL_DB (optional)

### Required Actions
1. Please publish the package to npm registry
2. Update package-list.json with the correct npm package name after publication
3. Verify the package can be installed via npm install @benborla29/mcp-server-mysql

Let me know once these changes are made and I'll be happy to re-review the PR.
